pr_title: gh cs cp: report error if no filename is remote
pr_body:
Some users expect that two filename arguments are implicitly local and remote (or the reverse), leading to a local file copy. This change makes it an error not to specify at least one remote filename. (scp is quite happy to degenerate into /bin/cp in this situation.)

Also, clean up cmdutil.FlagError.

Fixes #4579

If this pull request would close the issue, please put the word 'Fixes' before the issue number somewhere in the pull request body. If this is a tiny change like fixing a typo, feel free to ignore this message.

> Up until now we didn't feel the need to prefix errors; we felt that they are self-descriptive and obvious

Yes, they are perfectly clear; my comment was a mere typographic nit.

> I'm not exactly happy with the set of cmdutil.* errors and how they're handled in the main package. I've been reading this approach to error flagging and thought that it might be a nicer way to "tag" errors which specific behaviors.

FlagErrors are always shallow (they originate close to main in the call tree), so they don't seem to justify a more elaborate classification mechanism. I haven't looked at the other kinds of error yet---will do.

Ok, will follow up.

issue_context.title: 'gh cs cp file1 file2' does a local file copy
issue_context.body:
Some users expect that two filename arguments are implicitly local and remote (or the reverse), leading to a local file copy. This change makes it an error not to specify at least one remote filename. (scp is quite happy to degenerate into /bin/cp in this situation.)

We should probably report an error unless at least one file name has a "remote:" prefix.

Context: https://github.slack.com/archives/C02D0J5TVNY/p1634752044376500

review_comments: Perhaps there should be a FlagErrorf constructor too?

A constructor would be useful! Right now constructing a FlagError around the codebase is pretty verbose and seems repetitive. Without a constructor it's also easy to accidentally return a `cmdutil.FlagError` instead of a `*cmdutil.FlagError`; thanks for catching and fixing those 👍
